The part of the Roman Empire ruled by Constantius Chlorus under the Tetrarchy: Gaul, Britain and Spain. The map shows it in 300, labelled with a spelling of his son Constantine's name.

In 293 the emperor Diocletian split rule among four men to defend the empire's long frontiers. He and Maximian were the senior emperors; Galerius in the Balkans and Constantius in the far west were their juniors. Constantius ruled from Trier on the Moselle. His first task was to end the Carausian revolt, a breakaway state in Britain and northern Gaul, which he did in 296.

He was milder than his colleagues toward Christians in the persecution that began in 303. Constantius became senior emperor in 305 but died at York in 306, where his troops proclaimed his son Constantine emperor. That started the wars that ended with Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge in 312. Diocletian's own share appears as Rome (Diocletianus).
sum: The part of the Roman Empire ruled by Constantius Chlorus under the Tetrarchy: Gaul, Britain and Spain. The map shows it in 300, labelled with a spelling of his son Constantine's name.
